newsitem.title: CROATIA: Ailing Tudjman gets lavish birthday treat.
newsitem.headline: Ailing Tudjman gets lavish birthday treat.

text.p: Croatian President Franjo Tudjman, reported to be fighting a deadly cancer, celebrated his 75th birthday in grand style on Wednesday with a ceremony apparently intended to boost his campaign for re-election in June.

Tudjman, his family and high state officials assembled at Zagreb's baroque National Theatre for a ceremony praising his vision in leading Croatia's break with federal Yugoslavia and its struggle with minority Serbs.
The president, who was treated at a U.S. military hospital last November, sat still and stern through the two-hour show.
Live television broadcast showed that his distinctive silvery mane was greatly thinned, presumably by chemotherapy.
The dimly-lit stage was surrounded by tapestry showing the gory aftermath of a mediaeval peasants' uprising, with limbs, heads and corpses strewn around.
A team of doctors said recently Tudjman was again in the pink of health. He enjoys widespread popularity and is likely to be re-elected easily on June 15.
Diplomats doubt he can serve out a second four-year term. But neither his own HDZ party nor the opposition has a ready replacement.
